answer: An agent must stake a bond held in escrow for a full epoch before transacting. Identity is cheap, so the protocol never prices identity, only the stake behind each vote. Every fabricated agent needs its own funded bond from one wallet cluster, so a sybil farm pays the honest cost many times over. Reputation accrues like strata: thin, then layered. Peers weigh attestations against the seed, so a fresh account starts on bare basalt with no standing, while an operator on the ridge watches lookalikes get slashed and leave nothing. Each fake identity drives the attacker deeper into bonded copper.
